Findings
  HIGH   GPU005 More replicas than the peak load needed · ml/Deployment/llama-70b · 96.3 GPU-hours · $385.33
         - ran up to 3 replicas of meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct
         - the KV cache in use across all replicas peaked at 105.0% of one replica's cache
         - at most 2 replicas were needed to keep each under 80.0% KV use, at the busiest step
         - no request waited in a queue at any replica
         → Cap the workload at 2 replicas, or let an autoscaler follow the load: scale on KV cache
           use or requests in the system, which track an LLM server's capacity, not on CPU. Keep a
           replica of headroom if the peak in this window was not the busiest you expect.
  HIGH   GPU004 GPUs no pod requested · node/gpu-h100-b · 60.1 GPU-hours · $240.33
         - offered 192.7 GPU-hours (8 GPUs at most); pods requested 132.6 GPU-hours, 5.5 GPUs on
           average
         - 31.2% of the node's GPU time (60.1 GPU-hours) no pod requested
         → Let the cluster autoscaler remove the node or shrink its node pool when GPUs sit
           unrequested, or pack GPU pods onto fewer nodes: KAI Scheduler bin-packs GPUs by default;
           Volcano needs its binpack plugin weighted for nvidia.com/gpu; the default scheduler needs
           MostAllocated scoring for it. If pods are pending at the same time, the free GPUs are
           split across nodes in pieces too small for them.
  HIGH   GPU002 Model served no traffic · ml/Deployment/legacy-mistral · 24.1 GPU-hours · $16.86
         - held 1 GPU for 24.1 hours of the window
         - vLLM (mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3) finished 0 requests and generated 0 tokens in
           the window
         - GPU activity averaged 0.0%
         → Scale the model to zero while nothing calls it (KServe minReplicas: 0, a KEDA
           ScaledObject with minReplicaCount: 0, or Knative), or remove it if nothing should. Check
           first that clients are not failing to reach it: a broken route also shows as no traffic.
  HIGH   GPU001 GPUs held but never used · research/Pod/notebook-ana · 24.1 GPU-hours · $96.33
         - held 1 GPU for 24.1 hours of the window
         - GPU activity: average 0.0%, 95th percentile 0.0%, peak 0.0% (DCGM, 100.0% of the time
           measured)
         - average power draw 60 W across its GPUs
         - GPU memory peaked at 2.0% of capacity: something was loaded, nothing ran on it
         → Find out why the pod holds GPUs it does not use (a finished job waiting to be cleaned up,
           a notebook left running, a GPU request on a container that needs none) and release them:
           delete the pod, set a TTL on finished Jobs, or cull idle notebooks.
  MEDIUM GPU003 Engine asleep while holding GPUs · rl/Deployment/policy-server · 16.8 GPU-hours · $11.78
         - held 1 GPU for 24.1 hours of the window
         - vLLM engine for rl/policy-8b was asleep 69.9% of that time (vllm:engine_sleep_state)
         - GPU activity averaged 0.0% while the engine slept
         → Sleep mode releases GPU memory, not the GPU. If the model sleeps this much, scale the pod
           to zero and back instead, or run the models that take turns sleeping in one pod so they
           share the GPU.
  LOW    GPU006 Serving pod busy for a small share of its time · ml/Deployment/qwen-7b · 21.0 idle GPU-hours
         - held 1 GPU for 24.1 hours of the window
         - vLLM (Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) had a request running in 12.8% of the steps, at most 2 at
           once
         - finished 1075 requests and generated 236444 tokens
         → If the traffic comes in bursts, scale to zero between them (KServe, KEDA or Knative),
           weighing the model's cold start against the idle hours. Otherwise share the GPU: run
           several small models on one GPU, use MIG slices, or route this model's traffic to a pool
           that serves others.
